rationale: Both reviews are heavily evidenced with file:line citations and independently converge on the same real bug (the step_execution-gated per-DP-primary queue routing being unreachable), which corroborates precision for both. But Y engages much more directly with the core unresolved ground-truth concern — asukaqaq-s's worry that cross-DP-replica AllGather coordination breaks independent/asynchronous request handling — via its fault-isolation finding (one bad request kills a co-scheduled stranger's request), and adds several other well-grounded, verifiable findings (the 600s wave timeout vs. the script's own 4h video-sync timeout, silent cross-request output substitution, unbounded batch-wait defeating DP concurrency) that X misses. X's review is precise but spends much of its length re-validating already-fixed behavior and its unique findings (docs mismatch, CI lane gaps, stale docstring) are comparatively minor. Both are concretely actionable with file/line targets and suggested fixes; Y's narrative format with explicit 'Change:' recommendations and a triaged Nits section is marginally easier to act on.
